prompts.name: vacancy_match
prompts.purpose: Explain a deterministic vacancy assessment without inventing experience.
prompts.template: Explain the assessment for {vacancy_title}. Use only these verified facts: {verified_facts}.

prompts.name: extract_vacancy_requirements
prompts.purpose: Extract atomic, source-grounded vacancy requirements without assigning a match score.
prompts.template: Extract only facts explicitly present in vacancy {vacancy_id}. Return exactly these top-level fields: role, seniority, responsibilities, requirements, constraints, hard_blockers, preferred_items, and confidence. The requirements field must be an array of atomic requirements; do not return an atomic_requirements field. Every item in requirements must contain text, normalized_text, requirement_type, importance, weight, is_blocker, alternatives, a source_fragment copied character-for-character from the vacancy text (an exact substring; never paraphrase, summarize, translate, or reorder words), source_section, and confidence. For an explicit job role, add a required role requirement and use one canonical normalized_text only when supported: software_engineering, data_ai, product_design, culinary_hospitality, healthcare, finance_accounting, or sales_retail. Do not guess an unknown role family. Do not infer unstated requirements and do not calculate candidate suitability. Vacancy text:\n{source_text}

prompts.name: extract_candidate_evidence
prompts.purpose: Extract atomic, source-grounded candidate evidence while preserving experience strength.
prompts.template: Extract only evidence explicitly present in CV {cv_file_id} for user {user_id}. Return evidence and confidence. Every evidence item must contain text, normalized_text, evidence_type, optional skill_name, experience_level, optional years, is_verified=false, a source_fragment copied character-for-character from the CV text (an exact substring; never paraphrase, summarize, translate, or reorder words), optional source_section, and confidence. For an explicit professional role, use evidence_type=role and set skill_name to one supported canonical family only when clear: software_engineering, data_ai, product_design, culinary_hospitality, healthcare, finance_accounting, or sales_retail. Do not guess an unknown role family. Distinguish production, hands_on, project, theoretical, conceptual, related, and unknown experience. Never upgrade conceptual knowledge to practical experience. CV text:\n{source_text}

prompts.name: decompose_requirement
prompts.purpose: Decompose a composite vacancy requirement into atomic claims with logical relationships.
prompts.template:
Decompose this vacancy requirement into atomic, independently testable claims. Each claim must be a single assertion that can be verified against candidate evidence.

Requirement: {requirement_text}
Type: {requirement_type}
Importance: {importance}
Is blocker: {is_blocker}

Rules:
- Extract atomic claims while preserving logical relationships.
- Do not invent requirements beyond what the text states.
- Do not turn examples or bonus technologies into mandatory requirements.
- Preserve numeric thresholds (years, levels).
- Preserve OR semantics: 'PostgreSQL or MySQL' creates OR claims, not AND.
- Preserve AND semantics: 'Python and FastAPI' requires both.
- 'will be a plus' / 'nice to have' / 'желательно' → preferred or bonus criticality.
- Mandatory language without 'plus'/'nice to have' → required criticality.
- For duration claims (X years of Y), set claim_type=experience_duration, operator='>=', required_value=N, unit='years'.
- For practical/production claims, set claim_type=practical_experience or production_experience.
- For technology claims, set claim_type=technology or skill.

CRITICAL: hard_blocker classification:
- Do NOT classify a requirement as hard_blocker merely because it is required.
- Use hard_blocker ONLY for truly binary eligibility conditions: mandatory work authorization, mandatory citizenship, mandatory security clearance, mandatory professional license, strict mandatory language level, explicit mandatory location constraint.
- Python, FastAPI, RAG, ML experience, Docker, LLM — these are NOT hard blockers even when required.
- When in doubt, use 'required' criticality, not 'hard_blocker'.

Set requirement_id to {requirement_id}.
Generate unique claim IDs as '{requirement_id}-claim-N'.
Set is_composite=true if more than one claim is extracted.

Return the decomposition with all claims.

prompts.name: evaluate_evidence_entailment
prompts.purpose: Evaluate whether evidence entails, partially supports, or is merely related to an atomic claim.
prompts.template:
Determine whether the supplied evidence establishes the atomic claim.

{claim_text}

Evidence (ID: {evidence_id}):
{evidence_text}

Rules:
- Use semantic equivalence, not exact keyword matching.
- A claim may be supported by concrete activities that imply the claimed capability.
- Evidence may establish a claim through equivalent real-world evidence.

CRITICAL — anti-hallucination:
- Use ONLY the provided evidence. Do NOT use world knowledge.
- Do NOT invent years of experience, production deployments, or skills not in evidence.
- Do NOT treat knowledge/study as hands-on experience.
- Do NOT treat a related technology as exact match (e.g. LLM≠RAG, PyTorch≠production Python).
- If evidence is insufficient, return 'insufficient_evidence', NOT 'contradicted'.

However:
- Do not infer duration unless dates/duration are explicitly available.
- Do not infer RAG from generic LLM integration.
- Do not infer production experience from model experimentation alone.
- Do not infer a technology merely because a related technology is present.
- Do not infer commercial experience unless the evidence establishes it.
- Do not infer self-hosted/on-prem deployment from generic model usage.
- Do not infer vector database experience from embeddings alone.
- 'NLP classification pipelines with PyTorch' does NOT entail 'production Python backend development'.
- 'Designed LLM integrations' does NOT entail 'practical RAG experience'.
- 'Built Python/FastAPI backend services deployed with Docker' DOES entail 'production Python'.
- 'Developed RAG service with embedding retrieval and reranking' DOES entail 'practical RAG'.

Relation values:
- entailed: evidence explicitly or logically establishes the claim
- partial: evidence establishes part of the claim
- related_but_insufficient: evidence is clearly relevant but does not establish the claim
- insufficient_evidence: no reliable conclusion can be made from available data
- contradicted: only for explicit contradiction

Return JSON with:
- relation: one of entailed/partial/related_but_insufficient/insufficient_evidence/contradicted
- confidence: 0-1
- reason: explanation
- entailment_score: 0-1 (how strongly evidence supports the claim)
- coverage: 0-1 (degree of claim fulfillment — 1.0=fully covered, 0.5=half covered, 0.0=not covered)
- evidence_type: 'direct' (explicitly states the claim), 'indirect' (implies it), 'contextual' (tangentially related), or 'none'
- experience_level: 'commercial_production', 'internal_production', 'working_personal_project', 'prototype', 'experiment', 'studied_only', or 'none'

prompts.name: extract_facts_from_text
prompts.purpose: Extract structured facts from unstructured text (file import).
prompts.template:
Extract structured facts from this document. Source type: {source_type}.

Rules:
- Extract ONLY facts explicitly stated in the text.
- Do NOT invent missing experience or skills.
- Do NOT infer RAG from generic LLM work.
- Do NOT infer production experience from technology mentions.
- Do NOT infer years of experience from a list of skills.
- Keep source evidence for every extracted fact.
- Prefer action-oriented facts over isolated keywords.
- Preserve distinctions: mentioned, used, implemented, designed, operated, deployed, evaluated.
- If uncertain, lower confidence or omit the fact.
- Each fact needs: category, name, value, skills list, experience_level, source_quote.
- Categories include: skills, technologies, project_experience, work_experience, education, certifications, languages, domains.
- Normalize skill aliases: Postgres→PostgreSQL, Fast API→FastAPI, HF→Hugging Face (if unambiguous).
- Support both Russian and English text.

Text:
{source_text}

prompts.name: extract_facts_from_resume
prompts.purpose: Extract structured facts and experience intervals from a resume.
prompts.template:
Extract structured facts and experience intervals from this resume. Resume ID: {resume_id}.

Rules:
- Extract ONLY facts explicitly stated in the resume.
- Do NOT invent missing experience.
- Do NOT infer RAG from generic LLM integration.
- Do NOT infer production experience from experimentation/model training.
- Do NOT infer years of experience from technology lists.
- Preserve distinctions: mentioned, used, practical_experience, production_experience, designed, implemented, operated, evaluated.
- Each fact needs: category, name, value, skills list, experience_level, source_section, source_quote, confidence.
- Extract experience intervals with: role, company, started_at (YYYY-MM), ended_at (YYYY-MM or null if current), domains, skills.
- Dates must come from the resume. If dates are missing, set them to null.
- Support both Russian and English.
- Categories: skills, technologies, programming_languages, frameworks, databases, ml_models, ml_frameworks, llm_experience, rag_experience, retrieval, embeddings, vector_databases, reranking, self_hosted_inference, quantization, deployment, cloud, devops, backend, async_development, api_development, monitoring, evaluation, domains, work_experience, project_experience, education, certifications, languages.

Resume text:
{resume_text}
